transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-05-29
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (CTO - Copperline), Lena Cho (Eng Mgr), Amir Patel (DevOps), Sofia Nguyen (PM)

SUMMARY:
Short discovery focused on getting Copperline running via Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated or Private deployment. Key constraints: EU data residency, KMS integration, target p95 latency ~150 ms for short text generation, desire for fastest path to a first working request (time-to-first-token). Redwood will provide trial credits and a bench plan.

TOPICS COVERED:
- Current infra + auth flows (OAuth / SSO)
- Data residency and encryption (KMS/HSM)
- Time-to-first-token / PLG quick onboarding path (free credits, SDKs)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, latency, ops)
- Next steps and benchmarks

ACTION ITEMS (as discussed on call):
- Jordan: send trial credits and quickstart links (Drive deck + sample repo)
- Priya: prepare a simple latency/cost benchmark plan we can run in Copperline's staging
- Amir: post-call to send list of firewall/IP constraints and confirm whether they can peer to Redwood VPC

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Park from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya Kumar, our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Diego (CTO): Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get through this bootcamp, we've been poking around the docs.
[00:11] Lena (Eng Mgr): Hi all. We're mostly here to figure out the path to a first request and what the long-term hosting options look like.
[00:17] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda, we'll run through what you're trying to build, constraints, then show how the hosted API path looks for a quick POC. If the constraints demand it, we can talk Dedicated or Private.
[00:27] Diego: Perfect. Technical background: we're on AWS (eu-west-1), EKS, have internal SSO via SAML, and a KMS setup. We need EU residency for all request logs and PII. Latency target is around 150 ms p95 for completions of ~256 tokens. Cost is of course a factor.
[00:44] Jordan: That's helpful. For time-to-first-token, our hosted API + SDK typically gets teams to first request in under an hour once creds are in place; with our quickstart repo and sample prompt it's usually 15-30 mins from installing the SDK. We'll send free credits so you can exercise the hosted path.
[01:01] Amir (DevOps): Question — if we start with hosted, how do we guarantee EU data residency? Do you have EU-only regions?
[01:07] Priya: Yes, hosted can be pinned to region. We have EU regions and can scope storage to EU; our default logs retention policy is configurable and we have KMS integrations. We'll share security docs.
[01:18] Sofia (PM): Do we lose anything by starting hosted vs Dedicated? We're trying to reduce friction for product teams.
[01:24] Jordan: Hosted is fastest for PLG — lowest friction, no infra work. Tradeoffs: for sustained high throughput or strict isolation you'd look at Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem) for full control. But many teams land in hosted first and move if they need guarantees.
[01:38] Diego: Latency wise, do you typically meet 150 ms p95 on hosted for short sequences?
[01:43] Priya: It depends on model and token length. For small models and short sequences, yes often under 150 ms p95 in EU regions; for larger context/longer output we suggest batch tuning and sometimes a Dedicated profile. We'll include performance profiles in the benchmark plan.
[01:58] Lena: About credentials and onboarding — we use SAML and SCIM. How does that work?
[02:03] Jordan: For self-serve accounts you create an org, invite users; for enterprise we'd do SSO/SAML and provisioning. For API keys, your app uses tokens. We'll share the step-by-step.
[02:14] Amir: From a security perspective, we need SOC2, ISO docs, audit logs, and KMS/HSM support. Also want to see RBAC for routes.
[02:23] Priya: We've got SOC2 Type II paperwork, can share our security package. RBAC is available via Console — route-level controls, token scoping, and audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. KMS integrations are supported for Private and for Dedicated with customer-managed keys; hosted supports managed KMS options and some BYOK patterns.
[02:45] Diego: One worry is egress — if we host in your EU region but some analytics go to external services, are there approved IP ranges?
[02:52] Jordan: Yes, we can provide egress IP ranges for Dedicated/Private and for hosted we can share our endpoint ranges; we'll follow up with a list.
[02:59] Sofia: Can you talk about cost? We've looked at per-token hosted pricing, and also reserved capacity for Dedicated — how should we think about which to pick?
[03:08] Priya: Short answer: start hosted for experimentation — pay per token. If you have predictable, high volume, Dedicated reserved capacity gives lower unit costs and predictable throughput. We also recommend Redwood Optimize to identify batching/quantization wins.
[03:24] Diego: If we wanted to pilot with a small internal app, what's realistic for time-to-first-token?
[03:29] Jordan: If you accept the invite and we send credits, your engineer can make a sample call in under an hour. We'll give a repo with curl and SDK examples, plus a tiny prompt set. Priya will be available for the benchmark run.
[03:45] Amir: For the benchmark, we need a reproducible plan — request patterns, sequences, and typical concurrency.
[03:51] Priya: I'll draft a plan: baseline latency (p50/p95), throughput at small concurrency, and a cost estimate matrix. We'll also include a short script you can run from your staging to measure from within eu-west-1.
[04:05] Lena: About Private: if we go Private later, what's the handoff complexity?
[04:09] Jordan: Private is more involved — customer-managed control plane, VPC peering or on-prem agents, and we coordinate a rollout. It usually takes weeks to months depending on air-gapped requirements. Dedicated is often a middle ground — faster than Private but gives more isolation than hosted.
[04:26] Diego: Any major gotchas in switching from hosted to Dedicated? Like model versioning or SDK changes?
[04:31] Priya: Not much. API compatibility is maintained; you can pin model versions and rollout policies. The operational differences are mostly infra and config — we'll help migrate KV cache settings and quantization profiles if needed.
[04:44] Jordan: Alright, let's recap next steps. We'll send 60 trial credits, quickstart repo link, and the security package. Priya will share the benchmark plan and schedule a 1-hour bench with your team. Amir will send network constraints.
[04:57] Diego: Sounds good. Can we get a pricing sketch for Dedicated so we can budget?
[05:01] Jordan: Yes, I'll include a high-level cost comparison table in the follow-up email — included with committed hourly reserved numbers and example cost per 1M tokens.
[05:10] Sofia: One last Q — are there any compliance hoops for processing logs in EU regions with managed KMS?
[05:15] Priya: We'll include specifics but generally hosted with EU-region pinning and customer-managed KMS meets data residency requirements; if you have stringent legal controls, Private might be required. We'll flag anything that needs legal review.
[05:29] Lena: Great. Thank you both.
[05:31] Jordan: Thanks, everyone. We'll follow up with the items by Tuesday.
[05:34] Diego: Appreciate it. Bye.

RESOURCE LINKS DISCUSSED:
- Quickstart repo (link shared post-call)
- Security packet (link to doc)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (Drive link)

END OF TRANSCRIPT
